--- title: "Lorem ipsum: a Quarto field notebook" author: Max Thomasberger subtitle: "An executable R publishing showcase" description: "A public design showcase for typography, executable R, figures, citations, and interactive charts." date: "2026-10-26" categories: [showcase] draft: false bibliography: references.bib number-sections: true body-classes: article-tufte reference-location: margin citation-location: margin format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 2 toc-location: body mermaid: theme: neutral code-fold: true code-summary: "Show R code" code-tools: true code-line-numbers: true code-annotations: below citations-hover: true footnotes-hover: true lightbox: true execute: message: false warning: false --- ::: {.callout-note} ## Design showcase This page is a public design and publishing demonstration for feedback, using placeholder prose and entirely synthetic data. It is not a finished research article and makes no investment claims. The examples execute locally with R, knitr, ggplot2, DT, and Plotly. ::: ## Prose and structure {#sec-prose} Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Integer posuere erat a ante venenatis dapibus posuere velit aliquet. Donec ullamcorper nulla non metus auctor fringilla. Aenean lacinia bibendum nulla sed consectetur. **Strong emphasis**, *quiet emphasis*, ~~deleted text~~, and `inline code` can sit beside ordinary prose. A footnote adds a small aside without breaking the paragraph.[^placeholder] [^placeholder]: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. This footnote demonstrates the reading experience; it is not a research reference. > Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed posuere > consectetur est at lobortis. A research note : A short definition can live directly in the article. A computational article : Prose, source code, and evaluated output travel together. - Introduce the question. - Show enough code to reproduce the calculation. - Explain what the outputs mean. 1. Prepare inputs. 2. Compute a result. 3. Review the evidence. ### An aside in the margin ::: {.column-margin} **Margin note.** Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Quarto can place short annotations beside the main text on wide screens. ::: Cras mattis consectetur purus sit amet fermentum. Maecenas faucibus mollis interdum. Nulla vitae elit libero, a pharetra augue. Praesent commodo cursus magna, vel scelerisque nisl consectetur et. ## Executable R and inline results {#sec-computation} This paragraph contains evaluated R: the example has 252 observations, with a sample mean of -0.0244. The values are computed from the same data used in @fig-path and @tbl-summary. R itself is documented by @R. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Vestibulum id ligula porta felis euismod semper. Etiam porta sem malesuada magna mollis euismod. Curabitur blandit tempus porttitor. ### Folded code and tabular output The disclosure below contains executable code. The page's **Code** menu can show or hide all code and display the article source. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} knitr::kable(head(research, 6), digits = 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | day| innovation| path| |---:|----------:|-----:| | 1| 1.371| 1.371| | 2| -0.565| 0.806| | 3| 0.363| 1.169| | 4| 0.633| 1.802| | 5| 0.404| 2.207| | 6| -0.106| 2.100| ::: ::: ### Annotated code The explanations stay below the code on every screen size. Select a numbered explanation to highlight its line; copy the code using the separate toolbar. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} centered <- research$innovation - mean(research$innovation) # <1> round(sd(centered), 3) # <2> ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.974 ``` ::: ::: 1. Subtract the sample mean from every simulated observation. 2. Compute the sample standard deviation and print a compact result. ## Figures and cross-references {#sec-figures} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ggplot2) ggplot(research, aes(day, path)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = palette$muted, linewidth = 0.4) + geom_line(colour = copper, linewidth = 0.7) + labs(x = "Observation", y = "Cumulative sum") + theme_blechturm("light") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![An accumulated sequence of simulated normal draws.](index_files/figure-html/fig-path-1.png){#fig-path fig-alt='A copper line showing the cumulative sum of 252 simulated normal observations.' width=768} ::: ::: @fig-path is numbered automatically. Click the image to try the lightbox. A cross-reference such as @sec-computation also follows the section if it moves. ### Side-by-side figures ::: {#fig-diagnostics .cell layout-ncol="2"} ```{.r .cell-code} par( bg = paper, fg = ink, col.axis = ink, col.lab = ink, mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1) ) hist(research$innovation, breaks = 20, col = "#cba092", border = paper, main = "", xlab = "Innovation", ylab = "Count") qqnorm(research$innovation, main = "", pch = 16, cex = 0.6, col = copper) qqline(research$innovation, col = ink) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Distribution](index_files/figure-html/fig-diagnostics-1.png){#fig-diagnostics-1 fig-alt='A histogram of simulated normal observations.' width=384} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Normal Q-Q plot](index_files/figure-html/fig-diagnostics-2.png){#fig-diagnostics-2 fig-alt='A normal quantile plot of the same observations, with a reference line.' width=384} ::: Two diagnostic views of the synthetic observations. ::: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Duis mollis, est non commodo luctus, nisi erat porttitor ligula, eget lacinia odio sem nec elit. ## A shared plotting palette {#sec-plot-themes} Four accents share the publication's warm neutrals. Line styles identify the series independently of color. The examples below use invented signals solely to demonstrate the layout.
Copper Teal Plum Ochre
### ggplot2: the static figure This figure switches between two pre-rendered images when you change the site's light/dark setting. R runs at render time, never in the browser. ::: {.plot-light} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} signal_plot + scale_colour_blechturm("light") + theme_blechturm("light") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/themed-ggplot-light-1.png){fig-alt='Four synthetic signals A through D, distinguished by copper, teal, plum and ochre colors and different line patterns, on a light background.' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.plot-dark} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} signal_plot + scale_colour_blechturm("dark") + theme_blechturm("dark") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/themed-ggplot-dark-1.png){fig-alt='The same four synthetic signals with lighter copper, teal, plum and ochre colors and different line patterns, on a charcoal background.' width=768} ::: ::: ::: ### Plotly: the interactive companion Hover to inspect a value, drag to zoom, double-click to reset, or click a legend entry to hide a series. The same page theme switch updates chart backgrounds, text, and trace colors without recomputing the data. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- plotly::plot_ly() series_names <- levels(signals$series) line_styles <- c("solid", "dash", "dot", "dashdot") for (i in seq_along(series_names)) { rows <- signals$series == series_names[i] p <- plotly::add_trace( p, x = signals$day[rows], y = signals$value[rows], name = series_names[i], type = "scatter", mode = "lines", line = list(color = palette$series[[i]], dash = line_styles[i], width = 2), hovertemplate = "Observation %{x}
Signal %{y:.2f}%{fullData.name}" ) } p <- plotly::layout(p, xaxis = list(title = "Observation"), yaxis = list(title = "Synthetic signal")) plotly_blechturm(p) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.column-margin} **Two renderers, one palette.** The static version remains useful in feeds and documents. Plotly provides inspection controls within this static website. ::: ## Tables, static and interactive {#sec-tables} ::: {#tbl-summary .cell tbl-cap='Descriptive statistics for the synthetic observations.'} ```{.r .cell-code} summary_table <- data.frame( Statistic = c("Count", "Mean", "Standard deviation", "Minimum", "Maximum"), Value = c(nrow(research), mean(research$innovation), sd(research$innovation), min(research$innovation), max(research$innovation)) ) knitr::kable(summary_table, digits = 3, align = c("l", "r")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |Statistic | Value| |:------------------|-------:| |Count | 252.000| |Mean | -0.024| |Standard deviation | 0.974| |Minimum | -2.993| |Maximum | 2.702| ::: ::: @tbl-summary is a regular HTML table, suitable for copying and reading in RSS. ### An R htmlwidget This second table runs entirely in the browser after rendering. Try sorting a column, searching, or changing pages. It does not need an R server. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} DT::datatable( transform(research, innovation = round(innovation, 3), path = round(path, 3)), rownames = FALSE, class = "compact stripe hover", width = "100%", options = list(pageLength = 5, lengthChange = FALSE, scrollX = TRUE) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: A static table remains useful when an interactive widget is unavailable in a feed reader, PDF, or other non-browser output. ## Mathematics Inline mathematics, such as $\mu = 0$ and $\sigma = 1$, works within a sentence. A displayed equation can have its own label: $$ \bar{x} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i $$ {#eq-mean} @eq-mean defines the sample mean used in @tbl-summary. ## Tabs and columns ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Interpretation Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Morbi leo risus, porta ac consectetur ac, vestibulum at eros. Integer posuere erat a ante venenatis dapibus posuere velit aliquet. ### Method The inputs are synthetic normal draws with an explicit seed. This tab keeps a methodological aside close to the main text. ### Reproduction Render this article explicitly to rerun its R code: ```bash quarto render articles/quarto-showcase/index.qmd ``` ::: ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Lorem Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Donec sed odio dui. Nullam id dolor id nibh ultricies vehicula ut id elit. ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Ipsum Praesent commodo cursus magna, vel scelerisque nisl consectetur et. Maecenas sed diam eget risus varius blandit sit amet non magna. ::: ::: ## Callouts and disclosures ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## A collapsible explanation Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. This panel holds optional detail while leaving the main reading flow short. ::: ::: {.callout-important} ## A methodological assumption These data are synthetic. A layout demonstration is not evidence about a real process. ::: ::: {.callout-warning} ## A limitation This page demonstrates rendering features; it does not validate a model. ::: ::: {.callout-caution} ## A reproducibility reminder Frozen computation does not detect changes to external data or packages. Rerun the article explicitly when those inputs change. ::: ## A native diagram ```{mermaid} flowchart LR A["QMD source"] --> B["R execution"] B --> C["Frozen results"] C --> D["HTML article"] D --> E["Article listing and RSS"] ``` ## Citations and bibliography The citation @R comes from the local R installation's actual citation metadata. Bibliography entries live beside this demonstration so the site's shared bibliography can remain empty until real articles need it. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Pellentesque ornare sem lacinia quam venenatis vestibulum. ## Reproducibility appendix - [x] Set an explicit random seed. - [x] Identify synthetic inputs. - [x] Keep executable source beside prose. - [ ] Replace placeholder text before publishing a real article. ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Session information ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Component |Version | |:---------|:---------------------------------| |R |R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24 ucrt) | |Platform |x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 | ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} | |Package |Version | |:---------|:---------|:-------| |knitr |knitr |1.52 | |rmarkdown |rmarkdown |2.32 | |ggplot2 |ggplot2 |4.0.3 | |DT |DT |0.34.0 | |plotly |plotly |4.12.1 | ::: ::: :::
